transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um… I guess what finally got me to come in is I can’t seem to keep my work in order anymore. At the cleaners, there are all these tickets and receipts and notes from the back, and customer jobs, and somehow they end up all piled together. Then I’m standing there trying to figure out what I’m supposed to handle first.

It sounds silly when I say it, because laundry is laundry, you know, but there’s a system to it, and lately my station just turns into a mess. And then someone asks about a shirt or a dress and I’m digging through papers like—well, like when my kitchen counter gets covered with mail, except at work it matters more. It’s been really frustrating.
When you were a child, were you often this disorganized too?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I didn’t think of it as “disorganized” back then, but my teachers used to tell my mom I was bright, just… scattered. That was the word, I remember that.

I’d lose papers all the time, or forget to turn things in even if I’d done them. And apparently I talked out of turn a lot—my mother heard about that plenty at conferences. I always needed reminders to finish my work, too. Funny, I can still picture those little folders we had in grade school, and mine was always stuffed with crumpled papers and permission slips. So, yes, it goes back pretty far.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on a task, even when you want to?

Yes, I do. Like at work, I’ll start going through the dry-cleaning orders for the day, and at first I’m fine, I’m checking the tickets and the tags and all that. But then a few minutes later my mind is somewhere else—like I’ll notice a label on a coat and start thinking about fabric, or I’ll remember something for choir, or something I need to do at home.

And then I sort of come back and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to be checking. It’s frustrating, because I’m not trying to ignore it. I want to do it right. My brain just wanders off.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that something will go wrong unless you check or arrange things in a very specific way?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in that way. I mean, I do check things at work because if a ticket gets matched to the wrong bag, then that’s a whole mess, and customers get upset—and honestly some people are very particular about their clothes. There was this one woman with a silk blouse who—

Sorry. What I mean is, I don’t think I have a thought like “something bad will happen unless I arrange this just right.” It’s more that I’m trying not to lose track of things, I guess. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Do these problems with staying organized and keeping track of things also happen at home?

Yes, it does, though the work stuff is what really made me come in. At home it’s more like… piles. Papers, receipts, little notes from the workshop, customer things I meant to keep separate—well, some of that comes home in my bag, which I know I shouldn’t do, but I do.

Then I’ll put it on the kitchen table “just for a minute,” and suddenly it’s all mixed together and I don’t know what I’m supposed to handle first. And I’ll start sorting it, but then I find an old receipt or a note and think, oh, I should call so-and-so, and then I’m off doing that instead.

So yes, it’s not only at work. It just feels worse there because tickets and customer jobs get piled up, and then I’m standing there staring at all of it like I don’t even know where to begin.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?

I’m not sure I’d say “many different things,” exactly. I mean, I worry about things like work stuff, whether I forgot something, or if I’m behind, but I don’t know if that’s more than normal.

Sometimes I’ll get thinking about one thing and then it kind of jumps to another—like bills, or whether I returned a call, or if I left something in the laundry room—oh, and the laundry room at our place has this machine that keeps eating quarters, which is so annoying. But… sorry, I lost the thread.

I guess I do worry some, but I’m not sure if it’s a lot or if it’s just because things get scattered and then I’m trying to keep up.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say depressed, exactly. I get frustrated, and sometimes kind of worn out when things pile up, but I don’t think I’ve been sitting around feeling down all the time.

I mean, some days after work I’m just tired and annoyed, especially if something got mixed up or someone was upset about their order—there was this one customer last week who kept changing the pickup time, and then I kept thinking I’d written it on the wrong ticket—but that’s more stress than, you know, being depressed, I think.

So… no, not really. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Have these problems gotten noticeably worse recently compared with how you usually are?

Yeah… I think so. Not like overnight worse, but it’s been really causing trouble for, I guess, a little over two years now—about two years and a couple months.

That’s when I started changing the business into this more boutique-style thing, with more details and special requests and… you know, people want things handled a certain way, and I thought it would be good for the shop, which it is in some ways, but it got a lot more complicated than before.

So I don’t know if I got worse or if everything around me got more complicated, but since then it’s definitely been more of a real problem.
Do you often feel tense or on edge even when there isn’t one specific problem in front of you?

Um… I’m not sure. I don’t really sit there and think, “I’m tense for no reason,” if that makes sense. Usually there’s something I can point to, or I start looking around and remember something that needs doing.

Like if I’m at the shop and it’s quiet, I might still feel kind of keyed up, but then I’ll notice the counter needs wiping or there’s a ticket sitting there, and then I’m thinking about that. Or at home, I’ll think I’m relaxing and then I remember the trash—well, not always the trash, just whatever little thing.

So… I don’t know if it’s “on edge” with no problem in front of me. I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Do you often interrupt people or blurt things out before they’ve finished speaking?

Yeah… I do that. Not all the time, but enough that people notice.

Like my daughter will start asking me something, and before she’s even finished I’m already answering what I think she’s going to say. And then halfway through I realize, oh, that wasn’t even the question. Same thing with customers at the counter—I’ll jump in with, “Oh, pickup is Thursday,” or whatever, and then they were actually asking about a stain or a missing button.

There was also this trainer—well, not like a gym trainer, more someone showing me a new system—and I kept answering before she finished explaining, and then I’d be answering the wrong thing. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I don’t mean to be rude, it just comes out before I stop myself.
Do you often have trouble relaxing?

I don’t know… I mean, what counts as relaxing? Like, if I sit down to watch TV, I can do that, but then I’m also sort of half noticing the laundry basket or thinking I should’ve called someone back.

But I don’t know if I’d say I have “trouble relaxing” exactly. Sometimes I can sit, sometimes I get up and putter around. My husband used to joke that I don’t know how to just sit still, but then he’d be the one asking where something was, so—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I haven’t really paid attention to it as a separate thing.
When you start worrying about something, is it hard for you to stop worrying even after you want to let it go?

Um… I’m not sure. I mean, I worry about things, sure, but I don’t know if it’s hard to stop in that way.

Sometimes I’ll be thinking about something and then I get pulled into something else, like if the dryer’s buzzing at work or someone comes to the counter, and then I’m not really thinking about it anymore. But then later it might pop back up, like, “Oh, did I handle that?” or “Was I supposed to call?”—not always worrying exactly, more like remembering things at inconvenient times.

So I don’t know. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m trying to let it go and can’t.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about things even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I’m not sure I’d call it excessive, really. I mean, I worry when there’s something to worry about—bills, work stuff, whether I forgot to pick something up—well, not pick something up, I mean like errands, you know.

But for no clear reason? I don’t know. Sometimes I’ll feel a little unsettled and then I’ll start thinking, “What am I forgetting?” but that might just be because I usually am forgetting something. Sorry, that’s probably not answering it right.

I guess I haven’t really noticed myself just worrying out of nowhere all the time.
